convoLines.text: "What are you hoping for? Not the big stuff. The small thing. I mean it."
"God, yes. That's the dream now. Eight hours of not being afraid."
"A full night's sleep. Not safety, not answers — just eight hours where nothing needs me. That's my whole theology now. Not that it matters."
"Still on what you're hoping for."
"Finally. I was wondering when you'd see my value."
"Forget I said anything. What did you want? That's the whole of it."
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Carmine always took the burnt piece. Said someone had to. I take it now."
"Sleep's gone strange. I rinse the cup twice at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Anyway." A small smile.
"Okay, that's my quota of socializing."
"You're a good listener, you know that?" A tired smile.
"Good talk. I feel like I know you a little better now."
"I asked Carmine about the talking-to-strangers part — Carmine's gone. ...Hi. Sorry. I'm not good at the talking-to-strangers part. Good talking."
Something eases in their shoulders. "Oh. Okay. That's... that's fine, then."
They pull back half a step — not leaving, just... further.
"Still on the talking-to-strangers part."
"Don't worship it, don't fight it. Just work around it. Like bad weather or a difficult neighbor."
"Well." A breath. "That's where things stand."
"Right. Done. Don't look so relieved."
They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"You wanted one full night's sleep — no waking up listening. Had it yet?"
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Still on that personal stuff."
Something in them almost softens — then doesn't. Not yet.
You show them American Persimmon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Yeah? What's up?"
"Good question." "You asked me that before. It's a different question now." "I dreamed Carmine was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"I'm picking up Carmine's share of the work. Someone should, and it might as well be me."
"Right. Go on, then."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"You said you're not good at the talking part either. For what it's worth — you're doing fine."
"So." They look at the fire for a moment.
"Still on that personal stuff. You'd know about that."
They hear the warmth in it. They're not ready to let it in.
"Not right now. I've got my own things to handle."
You show them Stinging Nettle — where it grows, how to tell it apart. They nod slowly, committing it to memory. "Good to know. Really good to know."
"I've got things to do. People to avoid. You know."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"This was good." They mean it.
"I tried the American Persimmon like you showed me. Didn't poison anyone, so that's a win."
"Come get air with me. I need to think out loud."
"I buried this before the Scattering. Seemed stupid to keep it secret." Nathan digs up a wrapped bundle — food, still good. (+1987 kcal to the pantry.)
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Sure — what's on your mind?"
"Huh. Let me think about that." "Last time things were different. They always are." "Everyone's choosing sides and pretending they aren't. I hate it."
A warmth settles over the conversation — they lean in a little.
"I wish there was more to tell. That's it."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"What's this about? Still on what's been happening."
"All right. Thank you for asking."
"Sure. I'll be around."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"We never did finish talking about the big questions — that was 11 days back. Still on your mind? 'They glance at the fire, then back. The quiet doesn't seem to bother them.'"
"Walk my trap line with me? Extra hands, extra eyes."
Jason shows you where they go to think. "Don't tell the others. Everyone needs one place."
"Still on the big questions."
"...Sorry, lost my train of thought."
"Hm. Never mind — go on."
"You feel that? The air before a storm. That's the village right now."
"I eat fast and leave early. Not hiding. Just — scheduling."
"We need something to DO together. Joint work fixes more than joint talking."
"...Actually, forget it."
"Okay. We'll pick this up later."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"...Where was I? Gone. Ask me something else."
